traits.leader.note: Sargent's Manual (sargent-1922, p. 352): 'a straight trunk ... destitute of branches for 80°-100° from the ground, short, comparatively small branches forming a narrow pyramidal, or in old age a broader spreading head'.

traits.leaf_area_per_basal_area.note: USDA Urban Tree Database (McPherson, van Doorn and Peper 2016, RDS-2016-0005), TS3 raw tree data: its 103 tulip trees: 0.201 m² of leaf a cm². Median leaf area over trunk area at breast height of its open-grown street and park trees 20 cm or more through, the trees the broadleaf median (0.167) was taken over.

traits.height_growth_rate.note: USDA Urban Tree Database (McPherson, van Doorn and Peper 2016, RDS-2016-0005), TS3 raw tree data, open-grown street and park trees: the median height of its 123 tulip trees (6 age bins, 8 to 76 years) by age bin, fitted (least squares, weighted by trees) as H (1 - exp(-k (age + 3))): k 0.025 a year, H 26.6 m. Bins and fit: plantgen-claude project-files/tree-shape/UTD-SIZES-2026-10-23.md, round5-2026-10-26/tools/utdfit.py (tree shape, 2026-10-27).

traits.crown_spread.note: USDA Urban Tree Database (McPherson, van Doorn and Peper 2016, RDS-2016-0005), TS3 raw tree data: its 78 tulip trees 25 years or older: 0.61. Median crown width over height of its trees 25 years or older (15 or older where it has fewer than 10 that old), measured open-grown street and park trees.

traits.crown_base_share.note: USDA Urban Tree Database (McPherson, van Doorn and Peper 2016, RDS-2016-0005), TS3 raw tree data: its 78 tulip trees 25 years or older: 0.18 (quartiles 0.13 and 0.38). Median height of the crown's base over the tree's height of its trees 25 years or older (15 or older where it has fewer than 10 that old), measured open-grown street and park trees, which are often pruned up for clearance.

traits.bark_colour.note: The bark colour chosen by eye for appearance (see its note), as a screen colour: it stood as appearance.bark [0.42, 0.4, 0.36], which is linear light, so the trunk drew pale grey to white beside photographs of the species (2026-10-23). It stands here in sRGB, as bark colours are picked, and the bark rule (tracheophyta) turns it into linear light.

traits.leaf_colour_autumn.note: Wikipedia, Liriodendron tulipifera (read 2026-10-18): "In autumn they turn a clear, bright yellow". Colour ours.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_max_m.note: Silvics of North America vol. 2 (1990), Liriodendron tulipifera (Beck), Growth and Yield p. 410: grown trees are most often 30.5 to 45.7 m tall, and old-growth trees on the best sites nearly 61 m. FNA vol. 3 gives trees to 45 m.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Liriodendron tulipifera (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): blade (6.5-)7.5-15(-23.5) cm long.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Liriodendron tulipifera (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): blade (8.5-)12.5-18.5(-25.5) cm wide, wider than long.

traits.petiole_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Liriodendron tulipifera (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): petiole 5-11.5 cm.

traits.leaf_incision.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Liriodendron tulipifera (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): the blade mostly has two shallow lobes at the top and two at its widest part, sometimes squarish and hardly lobed. Simpson p. 200 shows it lobed too.

traits.leaf_lobes.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Liriodendron tulipifera (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): 2 upper and 2 lateral lobes.

traits.leaf_habit.note: FEIS's tuliptree review (Griffith 1991, read 2026-10-16): "a tall, deciduous, long-lived, broadleaf tree".

traits.self_pruning.note: FEIS's tuliptree review (Griffith 1991, read 2026-10-16): in forest stands about 66 percent of the bole is free of lateral branches; Silvics (p. 410) calls the trunk clear of limbs for a considerable height.

traits.bark_texture.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Liriodendron tulipifera (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): bark light grey, thick, deeply furrowed.

traits.flower_size_m.note: Idžojtić, Dendrology (2019) p. 383, Liriodendron tulipifera: flowers tulip-shaped, 4-6 cm.

traits.flower_merosity.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 200, Liriodendron tulipifera: nine tepals in three whorls of three.

traits.corolla_shape.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Liriodendron tulipifera (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): flowers campanulate, the tepals erect.

traits.flower_colour.note: Idžojtić, Dendrology (2019) p. 383, Liriodendron tulipifera: inner tepals yellowish green, orange at the base. The colour is our reading of those words.

traits.stamens.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Liriodendron tulipifera (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): stamens 20-50.

traits.carpels.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Liriodendron tulipifera (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): pistils 60-100.

traits.fruit_type.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Liriodendron tulipifera (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): a samaracetum, many overlapping samaras round an axis.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Liriodendron tulipifera (read on eFloras, 2026-10-16): samaracetums 4.5-8.5 cm.

traits.fruit_colour_ripe.note: Idžojtić, Dendrology (2019) p. 383, Liriodendron tulipifera: ripe fruit light brown. The colour is our reading of the word.

traits.flowering_months.note: Idžojtić, Dendrology (2019) p. 383, Liriodendron tulipifera: flowers May-June, sometimes July.

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it, the books read giving no ripening months.

generator.params.note: Red alder's crown values (a fast, straight-stemmed deciduous tree), changed by hand: one trunk, as FNA describes it (single-trunked), a wider crown, short-shoot leaves on the angiosperm default 0.26 m card (its blades and long petioles; a smaller card grows more shoots than the string holds), its shoots spaced more closely than alder's (space_density 3.5) so the crown of narrower lobed cards keeps within the module limit, and path_half fitted so it grows to the height at 40 years of its reference (refitted 2026-10-24, 22 to 13, when the reference became the Urban Tree Database's open-grown tulip trees, 23 m at 40 years). Not fitted to crown measurements. Its trunk is the pipe model's from its leaves, by the broadleaf trees' rules (2026-10-23). Its crown's width is the broadleaf trees' rule from the measured width over height of open-grown trees of its lineage (crown_spread, USDA Urban Tree Database) since 2026-10-23, in place of a hand-set crown_radius. Its crown's base is the broadleaf trees' rule from the measured share of the tree's height below its crown (crown_base_share, USDA Urban Tree Database), and its stem divides only where its flora or photographs say its leader is lost or that it stands on several stems, since 2026-10-24, in place of hand-set crown_base and fork values.

allometry.note: USDA Forest Service Urban Tree Database (McPherson, van Doorn and Peper 2016, RDS-2016-0005, public domain): its fitted age-to-dbh and dbh-to-height equations for tulip tree in the Sacramento Valley region (Sacramento, CA; 56 open-grown park and street trees aged 2.1-140.8 years, the database's largest and oldest set of them), evaluated: 23.2 m and 59 cm at 40 years. Was Silvics of North America vol. 2 (1990), table 1 p. 411: dominant trees of unthinned stands on site index 30 m, 27.1 m and 37 cm at 40 years; stand-grown, so thinner than an open-grown tree of their height.

appearance.note: By eye, after FNA vol. 3: light grey, deeply furrowed bark; bright green leaves, squarish with two shallow lobes at the tip and two at the sides, on a long petiole (5-11.5 cm against a blade 7.5-15 cm); drawn on the palmate card with five lobes, the card's odd count nearest the leaf's four lobes and notched tip, its broad, short lobes cut 0.3 of the radius, so the blade is drawn a little broader than long (FNA: blade 7.5-15 cm, 12.5-18.5 cm wide), against iNaturalist photographs of its squarish leaf (observations 240131367, 173949336); deeper sinuses fit the width better but draw narrow, pointed lobes the leaf does not have.

traits.fruitlets.note: Woody Plant Seed Manual, Liriodendron (read 2026-10-17): an elongated cone of closely overlapped, dry, woody, winged carpels, 80 to 100 to a cone; FNA vol. 3 (via a SEINet mirror) 'samaracetums 4.5-8.5 cm, samaras imbricate, 3-5.5 cm'.
